name: Carbon/LiCoO2 lithium-ion rechargeable cell
summary: Sony began selling rechargeable lithium-ion cells around 1991, shuttling lithium ions between a carbon electrode and lithium cobalt oxide; the design now powers most portable electronics.
description: A rechargeable lithium-ion cell with a carbon-based negative electrode and lithium-cobalt-oxide positive electrode, shuttling lithium ions between host materials rather than using a lithium-metal negative electrode.
tier_reason: The scoped record is a particular configuration, local witness, trial or material application. Dependence across fields or generations on THIS referent is not established; do not inherit the importance of its broader missing family.

impact.note: A lighter, denser rechargeable cell now carried by most of humanity in phones; portable electronics and electric-vehicle battery work grew from it.

why: Japanese makers of camcorders and mobile phones wanted lighter batteries holding more energy than nickel-cadmium cells.

market.note: Commercial applicability is established without establishing the worldwide first transaction.

evidence.locator: Commercialization and anode paragraphs; prior-lithium table
evidence.supports: The review describes Sony LiCoO2 and hard-carbon rechargeable cells and earlier lithium-metal cells.
Sony says it produced and marketed lithium-ion batteries in 1990.

This independent review dates commercialization to 1990.
The 2009 book distinguishes 1990 soft-carbon pilot cells and 1991 hard-carbon production.

events.statement: Sony commercialized rechargeable lithium-ion batteries by 1991, according to its 2015 account and a technical history.
events.scope: Early Sony rechargeable lithium-ion cells using a carbon negative electrode and lithium-cobalt-oxide positive electrode.
events.population: Buyers of Sony rechargeable lithium-ion cells
events.caveats: Sony’s 1997 report and a 2020 review say 1990 production/marketing or commercialization; a 2008 Sony release says market introduction was 1992. The meaning of marketing, samples and first paid sale is unresolved. Earlier Li-Al/TiS2 rechargeable cells and earlier carbon-host research existed. Ozawa distinguishes 1990 soft-carbon pilot cells from 1991 hard-carbon cells; exact product identities and buyer dates remain unresolved.
